name: Marxist Socialism
summary: Marxist socialism holds that history is driven by class struggle rooted in how society produces goods, that capitalist profit comes from the exploitation of wage labour, and that the working class must overthrow capitalist rule and replace private ownership of the means of production with common ownership and planned production for need. The state is understood as a class instrument that a transitional workers' state uses before it withers away into a classless, stateless, moneyless society.
scope: The classical Marx and Engels core: the Communist Manifesto, the Critique of the Gotha Programme, Marx on the Paris Commune and Engels's Socialism: Utopian and Scientific, read through the Stanford Encyclopedia and Wikipedia accounts. It excludes the later disputes among Marxist-Leninist, Trotskyist, council-communist and social-democratic strands, which are marked low or neutral where they split.

sources.author: Friedrich Engels
sources.usedFor: Anarchy of production, planning, crises, state ownership and the withering away of the state.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Marx's Gotha critique lists health services among common needs met from the social product before individual distribution, so guaranteed public care fits the program.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Marxists back struggles to improve workers' pay as reforms, though they hold that no wage level ends exploitation; the sources never address minimum wages, so this is inferred.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Engels argues that market production is an anarchy in which competition's laws rule producers like natural laws, to be replaced by social planning.

public-ownership.rationale: The Manifesto's measures centralise credit, transport, communications and factories in the state during the transition, and aim at common ownership of the means of production.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The Manifesto lists a heavy progressive or graduated income tax among its first measures for advanced countries.

unions-good.rationale: Marxists treat workers' combination as a step in class organisation, but the opened sources say little about unions, and Marx also saw them as insufficient alone.

property-fundamental.rationale: The Manifesto sums up communist theory in one sentence: abolition of private property.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Marxists would accept tighter regulation as a reform but, per Engels, state control of trusts leaves their capitalist character intact; the sources never address regulation directly.

cut-welfare.rationale: Marx counts schools and health services among social needs paid from the common product, so cutting them on dependency grounds contradicts the program.

worker-ownership.rationale: Marx praised cooperative production under a common plan as possible communism, though he wanted ownership by society as a whole, not firm by firm.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Marx's Commune stripped the police of political functions and distrusted the state's repressive organs; surveillance is inferred, not discussed.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Marxism has no settled position on drug policy and adherents differ; the sources never mention it.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Marx treated free speech and press as democratic requirements, yet modern Marxists divide on legal limits; this is inferred.

strong-leader.rationale: The Commune model rests on recallable delegates paid a workman's wage, the opposite of a strong leader bypassing the assembly.

state-harmful.rationale: Marxists hold the state is a class instrument that will wither away, but also that a proletarian state is needed meanwhile, so it is not simply unnecessary now.

limit-guns.rationale: Marx's Commune replaced the standing army with the armed people, so workers keeping arms is the Marxist presumption; gun control itself is inferred.

empower-police-military.rationale: The Commune suppressed the standing army and stripped police of political power; a Marxist opposes strengthening the bourgeois state's coercive organs.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: The Manifesto expects prostitution to vanish with capital but sources give no stance on its legal status, and Marxists split.

decide-locally.rationale: Marx stressed that the Commune did not break national unity but organised it, and the Manifesto centralises production in the state.

rehabilitation.rationale: Marxists see crime as shaped by social conditions, so rehabilitation fits, but this is inferred.

traditional-family.rationale: The Manifesto says the bourgeois family rests on capital and private gain and will vanish with capital.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Modern Marxists mostly support it, but it is anachronistic for the founding texts.

abortion-legal.rationale: Modern Marxist feminists mostly support legal abortion; the founding texts never address it.

more-religion-public.rationale: The Commune disestablished churches and sent priests to private life, and Marx saw religion as consolation fading with material change.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Marxists generally support anti-racist measures, though many prefer class-based remedies; this is inferred.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Marxists tie the family and women's roles to economic relations, but the sources do not discuss gender as such.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The Manifesto says working men have no country and expects national antagonisms to fade, so preserving national traditions is no aim.

gradual-change.rationale: For Marx, social structures that fetter productive forces burst asunder in revolution rather than change gradually within established institutions.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Proletarian unity across nations is a Marxist principle, so restricting immigration is opposed; the sources do not discuss immigration levels.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Marxists favour working-class internationalism, not bodies of capitalist states; inferred.

free-trade.rationale: Marxists deny that markets bring shared gain, seeing them as arenas of class interest; Marx also backed free trade as hastening conflict, so this is inferred.

nation-first.rationale: The Manifesto declares the workers have no country and ties emancipation to proletarian unity across nations.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Marxists distrust great-power interventions as imperialist, but the sources do not address humanitarian cases.

open-borders.rationale: The Manifesto looks to the disappearance of national divisions, which implies borders losing their meaning.

limit-growth.rationale: Marx praised capitalism's expansion of productive forces and saw communism as built upon them, though some readings stress ecological limits.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Ecological Marxism supports strong action against climate change; the founding texts say nothing on it.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Engels says productive forces become willing servants only once socially directed, so technology alone solves nothing without social change.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Marxism has no position on nuclear power and Marxists are split.

revolution-justified.rationale: Marx holds that when production relations fetter productive forces, the structure bursts asunder in social revolution.

experts-over-public.rationale: The Commune model was democracy without professionals, with officials paid like workers and recallable.

central-planning.rationale: Engels says anarchy of production gives way to social regulation by a definite plan, and the Manifesto centralises production in the state.

socialized-markets.rationale: Marx's cooperative society has producers not exchanging products, so markets are a feature to be superseded even where firms are collectively owned.

land-value-tax.rationale: The Manifesto wants land rents applied to public purposes and landed property abolished, not a single tax; inferred.

tax-inheritance.rationale: The Manifesto demands abolition of all rights of inheritance, which goes beyond heavy taxation.

basic-income.rationale: In the first phase Marx ties consumption to labour contributed, so an unconditional income is not his scheme; unaddressed directly.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Marxists have not agreed on protection; Marx's remarks on the Free Trade party suggest indifference to both sides.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The Manifesto has the proletarian state increase productive forces and direct industry and credit centrally.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Communism aims at common ownership, and small property is treated as something industry has already destroyed.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Marxism aims at a classless, stateless and moneyless society with wage labour ended.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: The Manifesto centralises credit in a state bank with state capital rather than abolishing the bank.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Marxism treats employers and workers as opposed classes, so state bodies setting wages jointly would paper over class conflict.

one-party-rule.rationale: The Commune was an elected council body, not rule by one party; Leninist strands differ, so this is contested.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The Commune was the antithesis of the empire, and Marx wanted officials elected, paid like workers and recallable.

democracy-best.rationale: Marx's model was a more democratic democracy with elections, recall and mandates, though he criticised the liberal form.

direct-votes.rationale: The Commune used binding delegates rather than direct referendums, and Marxists are divided on voting on laws.

workers-councils.rationale: Marx praised the Commune as a working body rather than a parliament, a model councils-communists later followed.

right-to-secede.rationale: Marx backed some national independence movements but expected national divisions to fade; adherents are split.

natural-rulers.rationale: Marxism aims to abolish class distinctions and treats rule as class domination, not natural fitness.

political-violence-never.rationale: Marx held that revolution is how fettering structures are replaced, so he did not rule out violence.

war-builds-character.rationale: Marxists see war as a product of capitalist rivalry and crisis, not ennobling; inferred.

separate-church-state.rationale: The Commune disestablished and disendowed churches and returned priests to private life.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Marx treated religion as ideology and a response to alienation, and rested law on class and economy, not scripture.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The Commune made courts elective and revocable public bodies; privatising coercion would rebuild class power.

military-superiority.rationale: Marxists oppose national rivalry and standing armies; this is inferred.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The Manifesto looks to the end of national antagonisms and organises by class, not ethnicity.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The Manifesto states the history of all hitherto existing society is the history of class struggles.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Marx criticised equal right in the first phase as bourgeois and sought distribution by need; the aim of classlessness points toward equality but not as a slogan.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Many modern Marxists support indigenous land claims; the founding sources do not address them.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Marxists see colonialism as capitalist plunder, but reparations are not addressed in the sources.

civilizational-union.rationale: The Manifesto organises by class across nations, not by civilisation.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Marx's alienation theory criticises egoism and treats flourishing as social and creative.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Marx criticised liberal rights as egoistic but never ranked duties above rights; inferred.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Ecological Marxists differ, and the founding texts treat nature mainly as the object of human labour.

limit-population.rationale: Marxists locate poverty in social structure rather than numbers, and distrust Malthusian limits; inferred.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Marx praised the bourgeoisie's creation of productive forces and said communism depends on what capitalism built.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Marxists favour developing productive forces, but under social control; the question's disruption framing is inferred.

human-enhancement.rationale: Marxism has no position on bodily enhancement.

algorithmic-government.rationale: The Commune ideal is democratic control by recallable delegates; algorithmic government is anachronistic.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Marxism has no settled stance on encryption.

restore-past-order.rationale: Marx treated history as progressing through stages and saw feudal relations as properly destroyed by capital.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Marxism presents itself as a scientific theory of history and class, so it resists treating ideology as optional; inferred.

direct-action.rationale: Marxists pursue conquest of political power through class organisation as well as mass action, not direct action alone; contested.

means-match-ends.rationale: Marx accepted a temporary proletarian dictatorship and forcible expropriation en route to stateless communism.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Marx held that communism builds on capitalist productive power, and he rejected primitivism.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Marx makes the end of individuals' enslaving subordination to the division of labour, including mental versus manual labour, a condition of higher communism.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Marx's Gotha critique states the formula from each according to ability, to each according to needs.

production-for-use.rationale: Engels says social production under a plan matched to the community's needs replaces anarchic production for exchange.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Marx holds profit derives from surplus value produced by workers beyond the value of their labour power.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Marx proposed a temporary transitional rule by the working class, though reading it as majority-backed democratic rule makes the 'dictatorial' wording contested.

collective-farming.rationale: The Manifesto wants public control of land and planned cultivation; Marxists later differed on forcing collectivisation.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Lenin and Luxemburg's imperialism theory holds capitalist crisis drives aggression, though not all Marxists say inevitably.

taxation-theft.rationale: The Manifesto demands a heavily graduated income tax, which presupposes taxation's legitimacy.

harm-principle.rationale: Marxists did not frame state limits through harm and are split on liberal principles; inferred.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Marx criticised liberal rights as protecting people from one another rather than building community.

conscription.rationale: The Commune planned short-service national militia, but Marxists split on conscription itself.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Marx's Commune made accountability turn on recallable delegates and voting power rather than flight.

state-as-business.rationale: The Commune tied officials to workers' wages and mandates, not to customers who can leave.

positive-liberty.rationale: Marx held political emancipation without material emancipation is incomplete, so freedom needs economic means.

media-academia-power.rationale: Marx held ruling classes control mental production through economic power, so economic owners, not universities, hold power.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Marxists explain social differences by social circumstance, but racial ability is not discussed in the sources.

organic-representation.rationale: Marxism organises politics by class, not families, communities and guild bodies.

total-state.rationale: Engels says the state dies out, so a state directing every life area is not the aim.

national-rebirth.rationale: The Manifesto rejects national framing and decadence myths in favour of class conflict.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Marxism opposes national rivalries, and later Marxist imperialism theory condemns expansion.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Marx treated feudal personal ties as relations capitalism rightly destroyed.

bound-labor.rationale: The Manifesto presents serfdom-like personal dependence as a pre-bourgeois bondage to be superseded.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Marx's theory of ideology holds the ruling ideas are those of the ruling class, though Marxists claim their own theory is scientific.

universal-morality.rationale: Marx treated morality and justice as class-relative and ideological, though his critique has moral force.

single-common-good.rationale: The Manifesto sees society divided by class interests, so a single common good hides class domination.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Marxists generally oppose nationalist state-building, but strands such as Marxist Zionists exist; inferred.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Marxism downplays national belonging; right-of-return is not discussed.

revive-national-language.rationale: Marxists treat national culture as secondary to class, but no source addresses language revival.

workplace-democracy.rationale: The Commune ideal of elected, revocable authority and free associated labour supports democratic control of production.

school-vouchers.rationale: The Manifesto demands free education for all children in public schools.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Marxism does not treat deficit limits as principled, but the sources do not discuss fiscal policy.

economic-freedom.rationale: Marx held liberal rights of property and contract protect isolated individuals and fail to deliver human emancipation.

rule-by-example.rationale: Marxists rest authority on class power and institutions such as recallable delegates, not rulers' virtue; inferred.

national-self-determination.rationale: Marxists are split between treating national claims as tools of class struggle and as distractions.

force-without-un.rationale: Marxists oppose imperialist wars but have no stance on UN procedure.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Marx called religion an illusion and presented his theory as scientific socialism.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Proletarian unity across nations means workers' provisions are not limited by citizenship.

work-for-welfare.rationale: The Manifesto makes labour a universal duty after the revolution, but conditional welfare under capitalism is not addressed.

class-collaboration.rationale: The Manifesto's core is that bourgeoisie and proletariat are opposed classes in struggle.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Marxists value culture's inheritance for the working class and the Commune opened culture to the people; inferred.

dominated-front.rationale: Anti-imperialist Marxists favour such alignments, others stress class over nation; split.

workers-nation.rationale: Marx's Gotha critique attacks the national framing of the workers' movement and the Manifesto says workers have no country.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The Manifesto sees the bourgeois family as built on capital and women as instruments of production.

ban-interest.rationale: Marx centralised credit rather than banning interest, and he gave no religious grounds for a ban; inferred.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Marxism organises around class unity and rejects legal separation of workers.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The Manifesto defines political power as the organised power of one class for oppressing another.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Marxism has no position, and ecological Marxists oppose while industrial Marxists favoured growth.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Marxists stress proletarian unity across nations, not national assimilation; inferred.

elite-replacement.rationale: Marxism explains migration and politics through class and capital, not conspiracies.

proportional-representation.rationale: Marx's Commune used delegation from communes rather than proportional party lists; Marxists divide on electoral systems.

national-mission.rationale: The Manifesto opposes national missions in favour of proletarian internationalism.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The Manifesto says the bourgeois sees his wife as a mere instrument of production, and Marxist feminists extend this, though class is held primary.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Marx called the state a parasitic excrescence on society, though corruption is not his focus.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Marxists explain traits through social conditions, and reject coercive eugenics; inferred.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The Commune made police and judges accountable and revocable; accountability for past abuses is inferred.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The Manifesto has the state take over production and credit, far beyond a minimal state.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Marxism denies national and racial barriers within the working class and treats them as divisions that serve capital.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The Manifesto aims to abolish class distinctions, but Marx called equal right bourgeois, so the answer is qualified.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Marx and Engels expected revolution across leading countries, but Stalinist and Trotskyist strands split.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Marxists generally see settlement colonialism as a form of capitalist expansion; contested in application.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: The Commune disestablished religion in public law, which suggests common civil law; inferred.

restrict-conversion.rationale: The Commune removed churches from state power, and Marxists treat belief as private.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Marxists treat such bans as religious law; the sources do not address it.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The Commune freed schools from church and state control.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Marx expected coercive functions to shrink only once threats from non-communist societies passed, implying persistence while encircled; strands differ.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Marx wanted rule by majority through elections and recall, but criticised social-contract liberalism.

trade-surplus.rationale: Marxists treat mercantilist goals as capitalist rivalry; inferred.

population-transfer.rationale: Class unity across national and ethnic lines rules out expelling minorities.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The Manifesto proposes despotic inroads on property rights and forcible overthrow, rejecting a non-initiation principle.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Marxism says class struggle, not competition between individuals or peoples, drives history, and criticises competition as anarchic.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Marxists have historically been banned, though they have also banned parties in power; contested.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Marx says workers are formally free to choose employers but must work for owners, a structural domination close to this principle.

separated-powers.rationale: The Commune combined executive and legislative functions in one working body rather than dividing them.

vanguard-party.rationale: The Manifesto casts communists as the most advanced section and class consciousness is needed, but Luxemburgists and others dispute a disciplined vanguard.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The Manifesto champions the propertyless majority, though Marx frames this as class interest.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Marxists favour social housing remaining public, but no opened source addresses it.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Strikes and workers' combination are central to class struggle, so legal limits are opposed; inferred.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Marx locates lasting poverty in capitalist exploitation rather than population.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Marxism sees social conflict as class-based and treats ethnic division as a divide-and-rule tool.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: The Commune used election with recall, not lottery.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Marx's dictatorship of the proletariat was an extra-legal temporary arrangement, but modern Marxists split on emergency powers.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Marxist planning accepts price controls for essentials; the sources do not mention them.

party-controls-media.rationale: Marx treated freedom of speech and press as requirements of democracy.

party-commands-army.rationale: The Commune replaced the standing army with the armed people under the Commune's control.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Marxist internationalism opposes citizenship barriers; inferred.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Marx's Commune paid public servants a workman's wage and abolished high salaries.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Marxist parties usually practise binding decisions after debate, but strands differ over how binding.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Marxists see capitalist supranational unions as bourgeois, though internationalism sympathises with supranational unity; inferred.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The Commune put the armed people and delegates in place of a head commanding the forces.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Marxism is indifferent to church governance, as religion is a matter for believers.

clerical-rule.rationale: Marx treated religion as an illusion that fades, so clerical rule is incompatible.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Leninists and Luxemburgists hold this and the Manifesto says workers have no country, but 1914 social democrats supported their governments.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Marx defended press freedom, though later Marxist states censored; contested and inferred.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: The Commune made officials recallable at any time and rotated, which leaves no room for entrenched tenure.

recall-officials.rationale: Marx praised the Commune's delegates as responsible and revocable at short terms.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Marxists oppose imperialist blocs but split on whether to leave existing alliances.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Marx expected property in land and housing to be socialised, not distributed to every family; unaddressed directly.

people-in-arms.rationale: The Commune's first decree suppressed the standing army and substituted the armed people.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The Manifesto calls for gradual abolition of the distinction between town and country, not for ruralism.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Marxists are split on reunification as a national claim.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Marx's Commune opened learning to the people; educated people as a class are not Marx's target.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Marx's stage theory and his praise of capitalism's progress conflict with a strict equal-differences view, so adherents are split.

death-penalty.rationale: Marx opposed capital punishment, but the sources I opened do not mention it; Soviet states used it.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Marxists back universal public education with modern content; sex education is inferred.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Marx treated religion as illusion and held scientific socialism; creationist teaching in public schools is opposed.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Marxism has no settled position on it.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: The Manifesto denies national distinctions and favours class unity, so descent-based citizenship is opposed.

minority-language-support.rationale: Marxists back equal treatment of workers across language groups; not directly addressed.

religious-exemptions.rationale: The Commune treated religion as private, so exemptions are unlikely; inferred.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Marx envisaged free development of individuals under communism, but gave no view on social conformity.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Marxist theories of imperialism favour cancelling debts, but the opened sources do not discuss them.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Marx held political emancipation cannot deliver human emancipation without transforming economic life.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Marxists differ between assemblies, councils and Commune-type bodies.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Marx made freedom of press and speech democratic requirements, but ML states disagreed; contested.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Marxists support international solidarity but see aid as inadequate to structural exploitation; inferred.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Marxists generally oppose national arms races, but the sources do not discuss deterrence.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The Commune had no head of state, so there is no Marxist stance on how one is elected.

central-bank-independence.rationale: The Manifesto puts credit under state control, so independence from government and a price-stability mandate conflict with it.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Marxists play down nationalist land claims; inferred.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Marx abolishes private property in the means of production instead of conditioning it, but the common good test points the same way.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Left-communist and Trotskyist Marxists say yes while Marxist-Leninists say no.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Ecological Marxists favour precaution, but the founding texts say nothing on it.

collective-defense.rationale: Marxists oppose military alliances of capitalist states, though workers' states made their own; inferred.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Marx supported self-rule for peoples such as the Poles and Irish, but annexation is not directly discussed.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The Commune disendowed churches as property-holding bodies and returned priests to private life.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The Commune had no head of state and treated rule as class rule; inferred.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Marxists differ between defending national unity and accepting secession.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Marx treats religious legitimation of rule as ideology and the Commune was republican.

flat-income-tax.rationale: The Manifesto demands a heavy progressive or graduated income tax.

character-from-environment.rationale: Marx's materialism makes consciousness a product of social and economic circumstances.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The Commune made all officials responsible and revocable under the people's mandate.

mixed-constitution.rationale: The Commune concentrated power in one working body rather than balancing few and many.

leader-cult.rationale: Marx's democratic model paid officials workmen's wages, but Marxist-Leninist states practised leader cults; contested.

equal-parenting.rationale: Marxism gives no position on custody law.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Marx's transition implies conflict until classes disappear, but the claim that party leaders restore capitalism is Maoist and contested.

land-redistribution.rationale: The Manifesto abolishes property in land and applies rents to public purposes; redistribution to farmers is inferred.

refugee-return.rationale: Marxists generally support return rights; the sources do not address it.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: The Manifesto looks beyond national claims, so claims by nationality oppose proletarian unity.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: The Commune removed religion from state power, and Marxists treat religion as a private matter.

women-must-cover.rationale: A Marxist rejects legal religious dress codes on women as ideological coercion.

common-currency.rationale: Marxists differ and have no founding view.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: The Manifesto organises politics by class rather than ethnicity or language family.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Austro-Marxists favour it while Lenin and Luxemburg opposed it.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Marxists stress class struggle where one lives, but strands such as Marxist Zionism differ.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: The 1859 Preface says the economic structure explains the political and ideological superstructure.

ban-cartels.rationale: Engels says trusts and monopolies do not end capitalism's contradictions, so breaking them up to restore competition misses the point.

no-bailouts.rationale: Marxists see bailouts as public support for capital, but some favour nationalisation of failing firms; inferred.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: The Commune made courts elective and revocable, so courts limiting a democratic majority are suspect; inferred.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Modern Marxist feminists favour parity, but the founding texts do not address it.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Marxism looks to international economic integration and proletarian unity rather than closed blocs.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Marxists support labour standards though doubt trade agreements; inferred.

moral-incentives.rationale: Marx expected labour to become life's prime want in the higher phase, but in the first phase rewards follow labour done.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Marx held revolution arises when production relations fetter productive forces and class consciousness develops, not by a small group's action.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The Manifesto abolishes inheritance rights and class distinctions, which removes hereditary privilege.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Marxists teach history as class history rather than national or civilisational; inferred.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Marxists condemn colonial rule via imperialism theory, though Marx called British rule in India progressive; contested.

patriotic-education.rationale: The Manifesto says workers have no country and aims to dissolve national antagonisms.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Marxists usually favour class-based remedies but support anti-racist measures; inferred.

public-money-creation.rationale: The Manifesto centralises credit in a national bank under the state.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Engels argues crises recur because the mode of production rebels against the mode of exchange, though revisionists dispute breakdown.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Marxist anti-imperialism opposes cultivating empire-era influence; inferred.

delink-world-market.rationale: Dependency theorists favour delinking but Marx held capitalism's global expansion creates communism's basis.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Marx saw workers as exploited under capitalism generally, though Lenin's theory of labour aristocracy is contested.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The Manifesto looks to unity across ethnic and national divisions, and the Commune made no room for discrimination.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Marx criticised liberal rights as protecting people from one another, so a bill of rights limiting majorities is not his model.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Marxist theories of imperialism sympathise with the claim, but the opened sources do not address it.

elective-rulers.rationale: The Commune's officials were elected, revocable and paid workmen's wages.

minority-veto.rationale: The Commune's mandated majority decision-making and party discipline make unanimity unworkable.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Marx justified revolution against rulers whose structures fetter society but did not use this constitutional language.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Marx praised the Commune as a working rather than parliamentary body, though a parliament against a monarch is progress.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Ecological Marxists accept it, but the founding texts do not address it.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Marxists are split on animal use.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Marxists treat paternalist duty as maintaining class rule, not ending it.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The Manifesto holds the proletariat must conquer political power through organised struggle.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Marx's theory of ideology holds that ruling-class control of mental production reproduces the existing order.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Marx held the ruling ideas are those of the ruling class and Gramsci extended this into hegemony.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Lenin's and Luxemburg's theories of imperialism, which Marxists take up, describe such transfers, but Marx himself did not centre it.

native-born-offices.rationale: The Manifesto denies national distinctions among workers.

party-own-road.rationale: Western and libertarian Marxist strands defended autonomy, though Marxism-Leninism resisted it; contested.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Marxists are split between autarkic and integrationist development.

return-lost-territory.rationale: The Manifesto opposes national claims as obstacles to proletarian unity.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Marxists support indigenous rights but differ on this claim.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Marxists treat fascism as capital's weapon against workers, but constitutional wording is not discussed.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Marxists reject equating fascism with communism; the sources do not address this directly.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Marxists see slavery as central to the conflict, but the opened sources do not address the war.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Marxists are not committed to preserving honours to figures they see as class oppressors; inferred.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Marxists hold historical materialism applies to all societies, so institutions follow mode of production not civilisation; inferred.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The Commune subordinated armed force to the people's own assembly.

paid-care-work.rationale: Marxist feminism argues domestic labour should be recognised, but founding texts do not address wages for housework.

filial-duty.rationale: Marxism has no position on filial duty.

office-by-exam.rationale: The Commune filled offices by election with recall, not examination.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Marx praised the Commune's mandated, revocable delegates.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Marx's Gotha critique funds social needs from the common product, which a private accounts system would replace.

land-use-tenure.rationale: The Manifesto abolishes property in land and applies rents to public purposes.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The Commune's budget arrangements are not detailed in the opened sources.

single-official-language.rationale: Marxists favour equal treatment of language groups, though some Marxist states imposed one; contested.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Marxists oppose capitalist land ownership generally, but singling out foreigners is a national claim; inferred.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Marx's alienation theory criticises acquisitive life under capitalism, though he did not frame it as consumerism.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Marxist states supported insurgents while Marxists also oppose imperialism; split.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Marxist principles of proletarian self-emancipation contradict it but Soviet practice differed; contested.

corporate-influence.rationale: The Manifesto says state power is the committee of the ruling class and corporations dominate government.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Marxists are split between defending national sovereignty against imperial influence and opposing state curbs on civil society; neither is addressed in the founding texts.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Marxists favour social policy for families but not nationalist pronatalism; inferred.

job-guarantee.rationale: The Manifesto asks equal liability of all to labour, and Marxists support full employment; inferred.

democratic-peace.rationale: Marx's followers hold capitalist democracies pursue imperialist war, so spreading democracy does not bring peace.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Marx treats law as class-relative but also demands transitional rule; adherents differ.

non-intervention.rationale: Marxists favour solidarity with revolutions and oppose imperialist intervention, so absolutism is not adopted.

industrial-unions.rationale: Marxists generally favour industry-wide organisation but the opened sources do not discuss it.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Marxism explains power through class and ideology, not secret ethnic or religious plots.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The Manifesto expects the bourgeois family to vanish, but Marx did not call for abolishing legal marriage.

public-access-to-information.rationale: The Commune made officials accountable to the people; a legal information right is inferred.

local-production.rationale: Marx welcomed world-scale production as a basis for communism and gradual merger of town and country.

informal-organisation.rationale: The Manifesto presents communists as an organised party, and Marx rejected loose anarchist organisation.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Marxists oppose national supremacy claims; inferred.

religious-nation.rationale: Marx treats religion as ideology, not a basis for community.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: The Manifesto calls for equality and unity among peoples, not tributary hierarchy.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Marx funds common needs from the social product centrally, not by region.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The Manifesto says communists do not abolish personal property earned by labour, only bourgeois property.

defeat-communism.rationale: A committed adherent opposes defeating communism as the goal of history.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: The Manifesto puts services under public control and the Commune opened schools freely to the people.

religion-illusion.rationale: Marx held religion consoles people in real suffering and fades once material conditions improve.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Marx praised the bourgeoisie's creation of productive forces and held communism depends on what capitalism built.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The Manifesto ties the bourgeois family to capital, so women's emancipation is bound up with abolishing it.

socialized-care.rationale: The Manifesto favours free public education and Engels favoured socialising domestic work, but care is inferred.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Engels contrasts scientific socialism with utopian small-community schemes and wants a national plan.

majority-settlement.rationale: Class unity across ethnicities opposes planned ethnic settlement.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The Manifesto's whole programme is communism as capitalism's successor.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Marxists treat such claims as nationalism; inferred.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Marxists reject denial, but the opened sources never address the Holocaust.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Modern Marxists oppose criminalisation; the founding texts do not address it.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Marx made press freedom a democratic requirement, but Marxist states suppressed opposition; contested.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The Commune removed churches from state authority.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Marxist imperialism theory critiques exploitation of colonies.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Marxists reject religious obligation as a political basis though they back anti-imperialist resistance; inferred.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Marx treats religion as ideology so religious law is no test of legitimacy.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The Commune model is a working body of delegates drawn from local assemblies rather than distant professionals.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Marxist feminism and its descendants say oppressions overlap, but class is traditionally primary.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Modern Marxists mostly support it, but the founding texts do not address it.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The Manifesto is built on the opposition between bourgeoisie and proletariat.

alienated-labor.rationale: Marx holds labour under capitalism estranges workers from product, activity, others and species nature.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Marx treats religions as products of material conditions, so none is inherently incompatible.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Marx treats religion as ideology and bases rule on class and the people's mandate.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: The Commune removed religion from state institutions, but dress rules are inferred.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Marxist feminists favour protection for women workers; inferred.

social-market-economy.rationale: Engels argues state intervention and regulation leave capitalism's contradictions intact, so a regulated market is not the goal.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The Commune replaced a standing army with an armed people, so Marxists oppose professional armies but not all armed force.

rich-first.rationale: Marxists seek class equality, but Marx also saw capitalism's progress as a stage; contested.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Marxists split between neutrality and aligning with workers' states.

dynastic-succession.rationale: The Commune made officials elected and revocable, which excludes hereditary succession.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: The Manifesto centralises credit in the state, not mutual banks; Marx criticised Proudhon's credit schemes.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Marxist theories of imperialism favour refusing such conditions; the founding texts do not address it.

property-franchise.rationale: The Commune's suffrage was universal for the people constituted in communes.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Ecological Marxist feminism holds this but orthodox Marxists do not.

reification.rationale: Engels says under commodity production the laws of competition act on producers like natural laws, which expresses the idea.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Marx held liberal freedoms mean little when the ruling class controls the means of mental production.

racial-franchise.rationale: The Commune's suffrage and the Manifesto's class unity oppose limiting votes by race.

online-participation.rationale: Marxism has no position, and the question is anachronistic.

open-government-data.rationale: The Commune made officials accountable to the people; open data is inferred.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: The Commune put religion outside state power.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Marxism rejects ethnic or religious division of working people.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Marxism gives no stance on sortition assemblies.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Marx held religion fades with material change rather than being reinterpreted.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Marx held that economic inequality undermines real democratic participation.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Modern Marxists mostly support equal rights for LGBT people, but the sources do not address it.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Marx argued education alone cannot remove religion because it responds to material alienation, so state promotion is not the route.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The Commune amputated repressive organs but kept a police made accountable; abolition is inferred.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Marx's democratic model is majority-based with delegation; inferred.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Marx funds social needs from the common product rather than private charity.

term-limits.rationale: The Commune rotated officials and made them recallable; formal term limits are inferred.

vote-delegation.rationale: The Commune used imperative mandates and recall, which resemble but differ from liquid delegation.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Marx treats religion as ideology, so religious offices are not his concern.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The Manifesto criticises the bourgeois family built on the husband's use of the wife; shared authority is inferred.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Marxist internationalism favours political inclusion of working-class residents; inferred.

rent-control.rationale: Marxists support limiting landlords' extraction, though Engels argued housing reform is insufficient.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Marxism has no founding stance, though Marxist-Leninist states used youth leagues.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Marxists are divided between anti-imperialist opposition to foreign weapons and support for workers' states' defence, and the founding texts predate nuclear arms.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Marxist anti-imperialism opposes foreign bases; inferred.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Marxists generally favour accountability for atrocities, but the sources do not address it.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Marx's first phase rewards each by labour contributed and the Manifesto says ownership of capital yields property without work.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Marx justified revolutionary force and did not hold absolute pacifism.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Marxists see nations as products of historical development rather than ancient essences.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Marxists honour revolutionary martyrs for class not nation; inferred.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Marx treats politics as material class struggle and religion as ideology.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Marxists have no founding view on diaspora homelands, and strands differ between Marxist Zionists and Bundists, so adherents are split.

culture-before-state.rationale: Marx's base and superstructure ranks economic change ahead of cultural change.

god-not-male.rationale: Marx treats religion as ideology, so its theology is not his concern.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Marxism organises economy by class ownership, not national majority.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Marxists split between supporting national unification and treating borders as secondary to class, and the opened sources do not decide it.

independent-unions.rationale: Western Marxists favour independent unions but Marxist-Leninist states made unions party-controlled; contested.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Marxism holds that the working class seizes political power and rules in the transition, so socialism without worker power is not socialism.

local-essentials-public.rationale: The Manifesto puts utilities and transport under public control and the Commune opened services to the people.

second-chamber.rationale: The Commune was a single working body, not a bicameral legislature.

municipal-property.rationale: Marx wanted a national plan and national unity organised through the Commune, not purely local ownership.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Marx stressed national unity organised through delegates, and opposed anarchist federalism.

family-wage.rationale: Marx's aim is to abolish the wage system, and his first phase pays by labour done rather than family need.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Marxists favour public funding for scientific progress; inferred.

person-over-state.rationale: Marx sought individual flourishing in community but denied liberal individualism; adherents split on this wording.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Marx's materialism treats spiritual life as ideology produced by material conditions.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Marx stressed national unity with delegated local power, so central power to withdraw it fits.

dense-cities.rationale: The Manifesto wants a gradual merger of town and country rather than favouring either.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The Manifesto organises politics by class, not race.

racial-pride.rationale: Marxism downplays race as a political identity; inferred.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Marxists oppose imperialist wars but support revolutionary wars.

language-defines-nation.rationale: The Manifesto organises by class rather than nation.

communal-electorates.rationale: The Commune's suffrage was based on communes, not religious communities.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Marxists explain politics through class rather than foreign plots, but the sources do not address it.

free-public-college.rationale: The Manifesto demands free public education, and the Commune opened schools gratuitously.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Ecological Marxists accept polluter pays but prefer planning; inferred.

future-generations.rationale: Ecological Marxists accept the principle; the founding texts do not address it.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Marxists attribute differences to social conditions, not women's distinct values; inferred.

arms-reduction.rationale: Marxists favour disarmament as part of ending imperialism; inferred.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Marxist internationalism opposes secret diplomacy of ruling classes; inferred.

capital-controls.rationale: The Manifesto centralises credit in state hands, which implies control of capital, though the sources do not discuss controls.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: The Commune replaced the standing army with the armed people, so arms stay with the workers.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: The Manifesto says workers have no country, so refusing wars between states fits, though strands differ.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Marxists support organised bargaining as a class struggle form, though not as a solution.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Marxists see subsidising low wages as propping up capital; inferred.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Marxists oppose self-imposed fiscal limits on public spending; inferred.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Marxist imperialism theory supports restructuring; the founding texts do not address it.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Marx calls the Commune's amputation of the state's repressive organs necessary and says the working class cannot simply take over the ready-made machine.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Marx refused blueprints but held that communism is the destination, so he did not favour open experiments with market systems.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Ecological Marxists criticise pricing nature as capital; inferred.

sacred-nation.rationale: The Manifesto opposes national mystique and works through class.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Marxists support free education so debt relief fits; inferred.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Marxists split on internal colonialism as analysis.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Marx used species-being but held human nature historical, so adherents split.

public-service-media.rationale: Marxists favour public media but fear state control; inferred.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Marx treats all religions as illusions rather than expressions of one truth.

farm-price-support.rationale: Marxists are split on farm support.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Marxists divide between workers' states defending themselves and the movement's disarmament demands, and the founding texts predate nuclear arms.

workers-own-party.rationale: Marxist theory holds the working class needs its own politics to reach class consciousness and seize power.

ban-fgm.rationale: Modern Marxists support banning it; the founding texts do not address it.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Marx would abolish inheritance, but equal legal rights for women are supported by Marxists; inferred.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Marxists prefer social planning over private tort claims; inferred.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: The Commune's authority came from elected revocable delegates, not hereditary or customary rulers.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Ecological Marxists favour it but orthodox Marxists differ.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: The Commune made judges elective and revocable; fixed sentencing is inferred.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Marxists are split on language requirements.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Marxists favour union solidarity, so opt-outs are opposed; inferred.

voter-id.rationale: The Commune extended suffrage broadly, so barriers are opposed; inferred.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: The Commune disestablished churches so none had legal precedence.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Marx criticised liberal democracy as insufficiently democratic when economic inequality undermines participation.

premarital-sex.rationale: The Manifesto criticises bourgeois family morality, but premarital sex is inferred.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Marx made freedom of speech a democratic requirement; inferred.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Marx funds social needs from the common product, not by replacing welfare with cash payments; inferred.

women-suffrage.rationale: Marxist movements strongly backed women's suffrage, though the opened sources do not discuss it.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Marxists locate women's oppression mainly in family and property, with religion secondary; adherents split.

race-social-construct.rationale: Marxists generally treat race as socially constructed; unaddressed in the sources.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Marxist feminists favour them but not as sufficient; inferred.

homestead-ownership.rationale: The Manifesto abolishes private property in land and applies rents to public purposes.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Marxists distrust courts of capitalist states but favour accountability; split.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Marx treats religion as ideology, so no scripture is inerrant.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Trotskyists defend nationalised property against restoration while others do not; contested.

indirect-election.rationale: The Commune's rural communes sent delegates to a central body, which resembles indirect election.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Marxists have supported autonomy for minorities, though Luxemburg opposed some forms; inferred.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Marxists split between self-determination by vote, as Lenin argued, and treating borders as class questions, so no single position is documented.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Marxists divide between accepting inherited borders for stability and redrawing them to unite peoples, with no founding text deciding the question.

simple-living.rationale: Marx wanted abundance under communism, though he criticised consumerism; inferred.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Marxists split between defending indigenous peoples against settlers and the Manifesto's opposition to national barriers, so this is not settled.

equal-conscription.rationale: Marxists split between opposing conscription itself and demanding equal burdens for women, and the founding texts do not address it.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: The Commune had elective, accountable courts; extrajudicial killing is inferred to be opposed.

close-ties-china.rationale: Marxists split on aligning with China, and the founding texts predate the question, so adherents hold no single view.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: The Manifesto rejects ethnic national claims in favour of class solidarity.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: The Manifesto abolishes property in land and applies rents to public purposes.

self-ownership.rationale: Marx treated labour power as a commodity sold under compulsion, so self-ownership alone is no basis for justice; inferred.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: The Manifesto prefers progressive taxation to regressive taxes; inferred.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Marx's common social needs are universal; inferred.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Marxism relies on organised parties and class organisation.

no-business-privileges.rationale: The Commune ended class privilege; inferred.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: The Commune put religion outside politics; inferred.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: The Manifesto looks forward to communism, not a return to ancestral order.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: The Manifesto criticises the husband's authority in the bourgeois family; inferred.

national-resource-control.rationale: Marxist anti-imperialism supports national control; inferred.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Marxists treat capital as a class relation rather than a national one, so blocking foreign owners protects national capital instead of ending ownership; inferred.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: The Manifesto sees the bourgeois family as resting on property and gain, so freeing spouses from fault rules fits; the sources do not discuss divorce law.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: The labour theory of value underlies Marx's account of surplus value and exploitation and no existing statement captures it.

missingStatements.text: The value of goods is created by the labour that produces them.
missingStatements.rationale: The labour theory of value underlies Marx's account of surplus value and exploitation and no existing statement captures it.

notes: Strands differ on the vanguard party, one-party rule, socialism in one country, the Soviet Union's character and national self-determination; those answers are low or neutral.
